saints.name: St. Anselm of Canterbury
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The father of scholastic theology, who sought faith seeking understanding…
biography: Born at Aosta about 1033, Anselm crossed the Alps and in 1060 became a monk of Bec in Normandy, drawn by the fame of Lanfranc. Prior in 1063 and abbot in 1078, he wrote in those years the Monologion and the Proslogion, with its celebrated argument for the existence of God.

His was a theology of prayerful reason — 'faith seeking understanding'. Named Archbishop of Canterbury in 1093, he resisted William Rufus and then Henry I in defence of the Church's liberty, enduring two exiles; during the first he finished Cur Deus Homo, his masterwork on the Redemption, and at the Council of Bari in 1098 defended the Latin doctrine of the Holy Spirit.

The long investiture struggle ended in 1107, when Henry surrendered the claim to invest bishops while the Church allowed prelates to do homage for their temporal holdings. Anselm died on 21 April 1109; Clement XI declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1720, and he is honoured as a father of scholastic theology and a patron of theologians.
saints.knownFor: “Faith seeking understanding” and the birth of scholastic theology.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1720)

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 21 April
